description: An eight-bit priority encoder: it reports, as a three-bit number, which of its eight inputs is the highest-numbered one that is high.

inputs.text: One of the eight inputs; D7 outranks D6, which outranks D5, and so on down to D0, so a high here is reported only while no higher-numbered input is also high.
Take this high to run the encoder. While it is low every output is held at 0V.

outputs.text: The least significant bit of the number of the highest input that is high.
The middle bit of the number of the highest input that is high.
The most significant bit of the number of the highest input that is high.
10V while the encoder is enabled and none of the eight inputs is high, which distinguishes no input at all from D0 alone.
10V while the encoder is enabled and at least one of the eight inputs is high.

notes: A logic input counts as high once it rises above 2V and does not count as low again until it falls below 0.1V; a logic output is 10V for high and 0V for low.
The enable input has to be taken high before anything comes out; with nothing patched there every output stays at 0V.
